purpose: Read-only capacity assessment of two disjoint S32 subtree workers during the sequential parent overview build.
decision: Keep the existing sequential builder running; no parallel subtree prototype or production transition.

snapshot.timestampPrecision: Measurement snapshot immediately preceded this report; no separate measurement timestamp was retained.

method: Read /proc/PID/status for the existing build_overview.py process and memory.stat/memory.max/cpu.max for its cgroup.
Read existing node JSON metadata only; use each highest completed node as the frontier, otherwise recursively sum completed descendant frontiers.
Compute other anonymous memory plus kernel as cgroup anon minus current builder RSS plus cgroup kernel; this is an approximate conservative planning baseline, not a measured allocation partition.
No source downloads, mesh decoding, numerical processing, builder interruption, or Builder/C edits were performed.
limitations: The measured high-water RSS covers completed work only; it is not a guaranteed maximum for remaining denser S16/S32 merges or the final root.
Frontier triangle sums are upper bounds before further child reduction and welding, not expected final S32 inputs or evidence that the 6M merge cap will fail.
Snapshot node files may advance while the running builder writes; these counts describe one read-only scan, not a stopped consistent transaction.
Process RSS includes some shared/file-backed pages; subtracting it from cgroup anonymous memory is only an estimate and may understate the other-anonymous baseline.
Reclaimable file cache is not treated as live working memory; the kernel figure is retained conservatively even though some slab may be reclaimable.

Two workers at the observed peak may fit, but unbuilt frontier inputs are substantially larger than the largest completed merge; two-worker peaks, orchestrator inventory, and headroom have not been bounded.
The existing leaf wrapper watchdog is not a hard instantaneous native-allocation limit; it cannot turn an unmeasured subtree peak into a guaranteed memory bound.
No parallel subtree speedup or byte-identity claim is made because no such prototype was run.
rationale: The serial build is progressing without cap failures. Prototyping, verifying, and switching orchestration now offers uncertain savings while introducing an unproven two-worker memory envelope under the 8 GiB cgroup limit.
productionControl: Root retains ownership of the active sequential process; no new production writer was started.
